title: ESP and how it fed into her music
summary: She says ESP should go into the music: she could hear the next note a musician would play. It cannot be controlled.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: This kind of sense that you had, entirely aside from seeing that sort of thing and reconstructing something that happened some place, how did it affect your music?

I think that when anybody has anything like that, ESP, if you're an artist it should be put into your music, because at one time I could hear a musician playing and could hear the note he was going to make next. It was just that fast. It was just like seeing spiritual or telling someone's fortune, I knew exactly what he was going to do.
This is why you could listen to Fats Waller improvise a whole score and then you sit down and play it?

Well, I don't know, but it may have something to do with the fastness of the mind and hearing. See, when you develop a thing like that it can be good for you or it can be very bad. You can use it in a bad way, 'cause there's nothing we can do about what's happening to us. Some people lose their minds. But I think it's useful in your work.
Is this something you can control?
